rationale: Eight feeds are waiting and the current single-worker setting cannot clear the backlog. All workers share one upstream account, so setting workers to 8 risks concurrent rate-limiting with no load-test evidence to support it. Four workers delivers a 4× throughput increase while keeping concurrency at 50 % of the maximum, preserving meaningful headroom on the shared account. No load test or account-limit change contradicts this level, making it the highest sustainably-supported choice from the available evidence.
